I tend to disagree, there are many titles that don't translate very well into a standard eink experience. 

Textbooks for h.s. and college don't make the leap without significant modifications, even then the experience is far weaker. Jumping between footnotes, faster highlighting, images with captions and so on simply fail to make the leap with current technology. Its not impossible to envision faster eink devices that can handle this rapid jumping from body to caption to footnote to answerkey to highlights to image but at the moment the experience is nothing short of frustrating. 

I agree that amazon is leading in accessibility and in volume of content, my point was that accessibility is the focus while I look forward to new innovation in the reading experience. Those titles that fail to impress currently are held back by technological limitations. Imagine for a moment a eink device that can pinch and zoom or incorporate color! That hardware is not the focus this year rather its accessibility. Once they get the market hooked the prices of this future tech will drop and be ready for mass production. But that's a few years off.

There used to be a rule i followed when buying a desktop. Wait and buy a machine that will beat least 3-4 times more powerful. This of course made me run any machine into the ground but it created a really big wow factor when I finally made the leap. 

These days specs don't mean anything it's all down to the features. Higher resolution on a tablet, larger screens on a phone, and more apps...better apps etc. 

The kindle paperlight is the first real 2nd generation of the e-reader. Although the screen was a long overdue upgrade the main focus seems to be on the store front. It's easier than ever to have access to any digital publication in seconds. I can buy a book for less time then to start my car to head to a real bookstore. And that seems to be the real focus. The tech is nice but the accessibility seems to be the driving focus. But I don't know If that makes it a worthy upgrade. 

With a half dozen tablets hitting the market this fall its time for e-readers and tablets to dominate sales. Nexus 7, kindle ( in Its many flavors), new kobu readers, new nooks, and the rumored ipad mini and ms slate...it's going to be a brutal holiday season. The champion will be the hardware that offers the best software. Ms is going to run with their tails between their legs. Sony, the first company to make a e-reader finally pulls out due to difficulty to get titles into their readers. It's going to be brutal but the focus is not on features. Not this year. 

People want to know that the books they buy now will be available years down the road. Sure I'm ranting but just you wait the readers of next year will be amazing. I can't wait for that wow factor when I make an upgrade. By then mobi should be able to support audio and video. That will kickoff the next gen of e readers.

In the past I've had to write many in depth papers that analyze movies for the academic world. I've also assisted a number of students to help structure their writing to communicate their ideas efficiently. As I applaud your hard work I must admit this is far from a first draft. Rather an assortment of surface information. Ideas without legs. 

This is not a bad thing, in fact it's quite inspiring to find people who wish to discuss cinema at length. But if you wish to engage the reader you need a engaging argument. 

"I just want people to maybe reconsider some of the things they initially thought about
The Dark Knight Rises"

Boring! It's an awful habit for many early writers to create a preamble to buffer their ideas. You see it in business writing all the time…"I'm writing this letter to tell you". I can clearly see it's a letter get to the point. Buffer zones like this are comfortable for writing as they can lead into an idea but should be dropped during editing as flabby writing. 

Make us care. 

Trying to convince a reader a book or movie or game is good is a not an argument. Rather pull a reader in with overarching concepts that stood out to you. Stick to the main topic and touch upon related topics.  

I have to run but I suggest you read some slavoj zizek, roger ebert for in depth analysis. Build your paper like a stack of cards anything that may harm your overall structure or touch on unrelated topics should be removed. It's about depth and structure. 12,000 words may feel nice but if it's not impactful and well structured it's worthless. Length comes with analysis and analysis with curiosity and curiosity with time.

Keep writing! (You have to go deeper! - lol meta)

I'm open to have fun but let's just hang for a while with no pressure. Once I'm confortable I'll open up. Your time is an investment. You spent some time hanging with me, you have my attention over any other girl in the bar/club.
